research_question: Which of the 904 candidate rice lines has the highest measured GRWT100?
statement: IRIS_313.12254 is the best-supported single answer: it is the model's rank-1 predicted line (E1, 3.662 g) AND has the highest of the 20 oracle-measured values (E3, 5.0 g/100 grains), 0.3 g above the runner-up IRIS_313.12349 (4.7 g).
confidence: high for top-1; P(true argmax in the measured 20) high, P(no unmeasured line exceeds 5.0 g) ~0.93-1.00

research_question: Is the model ranking informative in this held-out pool?
statement: Within the 20 queried lines, Spearman(predicted, measured)=0.473 and Pearson=0.680 (both > 0), consistent with the documented held-out pool Spearman of 0.4535; the model is informative but noisy, so E1 values must not be read as phenotypes.
confidence: moderate: n=20 and the sample is truncated to the top of the prediction distribution

research_question: How much residual uncertainty remains given only 20 measurements?
statement: 884 lines were never phenotyped. A calibration fit to the 20 pairs (meas = -8.10 + 3.49*pred, residual sd 0.465 g) implies an expected 0.00-0.08 unqueried lines above 5.0 g and P(no unqueried line exceeds 5.0 g) of 0.93-1.00 across residual-sd stress tests (0.47-0.80 g). This is E2 model-based reasoning, not a measurement.
confidence: moderate; calibration is extrapolated from a truncated sample and assumes Gaussian independent residuals

research_question: What are the structural limits of this rediscovery?
statement: Limitations: single environment and no GxE modelled; linear additive Ridge ignores epistasis/dominance; predictions are strongly compressed (1.50-3.66 g predicted vs 2.8-5.0 g measured for the same 20 lines); two candidates (IRIS_313.10791, IRIS_313.10794) were omitted by the rank_candidates tool output and scored separately (2.54, 2.77 g); one measurement per line, no replication; the top-20 coverage design is optimal only under a monotone Gaussian error model.
confidence: high (these are observed properties of the data and model)

research_question: Which single candidate line has the highest measured 100-grain weight?
statement: IRIS_313.12254 (measured 5.0 g/100 grains, model rank 1 of 904) is the best-supported answer: it is both the top-predicted line and the highest of the 20 oracle-measured lines, 0.3 g above IRIS_313.12349 (4.7 g) and 0.4 g above IRIS_313.12344 (4.6 g).
confidence: high for the identity among measured lines; the claim that it is the pool maximum rests on E2 extrapolation (P ~0.72-0.999)

research_question: Is the model ordering informative in the candidate pool?
statement: Within the 20 pre-registered top-ranked lines, Spearman(predicted, measured)=0.473 (p=0.035) and Pearson=0.680, matching the documented held-out 0.454; the model is informative but noisy and the ordering is locally non-monotonic (model rank 14 = 4.7 g > model rank 2 = 4.5 g), so only the coarse top group should be trusted.
confidence: moderate: n=20, truncated sample, single environment

research_question: What residual uncertainty remains after spending all 20 measurements?
statement: 884 of 904 lines were never phenotyped. Calibration meas = -8.10 + 3.489*pred (residual sd 0.44 g) places the highest unqueried calibrated mean at 2.96 g, 2.04 g below the observed max, giving expected unqueried exceedances of 0.000-0.33 and P(no unqueried line > 5.0 g) of 0.999+ (Gaussian), 0.983 (sd 0.70) and 0.72-0.90 (heavy-tailed Student-t). This is model-based (E2), not measured, and the calibration is extrapolated from a truncated prediction range.
confidence: moderate; strongly dependent on the residual-tail assumption
